title: Nut-Free Caramel Drizzle Cupcakes
shortDescription: Vanilla cupcakes topped with homemade caramel drizzle, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake, no nuts anywhere.
description: These cupcakes came out of a school bake sale request. A parent asked for something sweet and safe for a nut-free classroom, so I built this recipe around a simple sugar and butter caramel.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp flaky sea salt (for caramel and garnish)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and sugar together for 3 minutes, until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla extract.
Add the flour mix and milk in three parts, alternating, starting and ending with flour.
Divide batter into liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
For the caramel, melt sugar in a dry saucepan over medium heat, swirling the pan often until it turns amber.
Add butter carefully, whisking until melted. Pour in cream slowly, whisking until smooth.
Stir in sea salt. Let caramel cool 15 minutes to thicken slightly before drizzling.
Drizzle cooled caramel over each cooled cupcake. Add a pinch of flaky salt on top.
tips: Watch the caramel closely once it starts to color. It can go from amber to burnt in under a minute.
Do not stir the sugar while it melts, just swirl the pan gently to keep it even.
If your caramel seizes when you add butter, lower the heat and whisk steadily until it smooths out.
Make the caramel a day ahead and store it in the fridge. Warm it gently before drizzling.

faq.question: Can I make the caramel without a candy thermometer?
faq.answer: Yes, just watch the color instead of the temperature. Pull the sugar off the heat once it turns deep amber, right before it looks too dark.

faq.question: Why did my caramel turn grainy?
faq.answer: This usually happens if sugar crystals touch the side of the pan and crystallize back. Use a clean pan and avoid stirring while the sugar melts.

faq.question: Is this recipe safe for a nut-free classroom?
faq.answer: Yes, there are no nuts, nut extracts, or nut-based products in this recipe. Always check your specific brands for cross contamination warnings.

faq.question: Can I drizzle the caramel while it's still hot?
faq.answer: Let it cool about 15 minutes first. Hot caramel is too thin and will slide right off the cupcakes instead of sitting on top.

conclusion: This recipe proves you do not need nuts to get a rich, caramel dessert. The homemade drizzle takes a bit of patience, but it turns a plain vanilla cupcake into something special.
metaDescription: Try this nut-free caramel drizzle cupcake recipe with homemade sugar and butter caramel. Bake a safe, sweet batch today.
